{{Short description|13th century logical and author}}
'''Lambert of Auxerre''' was a medieval 13th century logician best known for writing the book "''Summa Lamberti''" or simply "''Logica''" <ref>The ''Summa Lamberti'' is now attributed to Lambert of Lagny (Lambertus de Latiniaco) (fl. 1250): see A. de Libera (1982).</ref> in the mid 1250s which became an authoritative textbook on logic in the Western tradition.<ref>{{Cite book|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=c2nmqagEz6QC|title = Mediaeval and Renaissance Logic|last = Gabbay|first = Dov M.|last2 = Woods|first2 = John|date = 2008-03-14|publisher = Elsevier|isbn = 9780080560854|language = en}}</ref> He was a Dominican in the Dominican house at [[Auxerre]]. His contemporaries were [[Peter of Spain (author)|Peter of Spain]], [[William of Sherwood]], and [[Roger Bacon]].<ref>{{Cite book|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=MOqtNYn8qzkC|title = The Cambridge Translations of Medieval Philosophical Texts: Volume 1, Logic and the Philosophy of Language|last = Kretzmann|first = Norman|last2 = Stump|first2 = Eleonore|date = 1988-01-01|publisher = Cambridge University Press|isbn = 9780521280631|language = en}}</ref>

==Works and Translations==
* [http://www.studiumanistici.unimi.it/files/_ITA_/Filarete/059.pdf ''Logica (Summa Lamberti)''], First edition of the Latin text by Franco Alessio, Firenze, La Nuova Italia, 1971.
* ''Logica, or Summa Lamberti'', translated with notes and introduction by Thomas S. Maloney, Notre Dame University Press, 2015.
* ''Properties of Terms'', in Norman Kretzmann, Eleonore Stump, trans., in ''Cambridge Translations of Medieval Philosophical Texts, Vol. 1: Logic and the Philosophy of Language'', Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1988, pp.&nbsp;102–162.
* Alain de Libera, ''Le traité De appellatione de Lambert de Lagny (Lambert d’Auxerre)'', Archives d’histoire doctrinale et littéraire du Moyen Age, 48, pp.&nbsp;227–285, 1982.

==Further reading==
* L. M. de Rijk, ''On the genuine text of Peter of Spain’s Summule logicales, IV: The Lectura tractatuum by Guillelmus Arnaldi, master of arts at Toulouse (1235–1244). With a note on the date of Lambert of Auxerre’s Summule''. Vivarium 7, 1969, pp.&nbsp;120–162.
* A. de Libera, ''De la logique à la grammaire: remarques sur la théorie de la détermination chez Roger Bacon et Lambert d’Auxerre (Lambert de Lagny)'', In: Geoffrey L. Bursill-Hall, Sten Ebbesen and E.F.K. Koerner (eds.), ''De Ortu Grammaticae. Studies in Medieval Grammar and Linguistic Theory in Memory of Jan Pinborg'', John Benjamin, Amsterdam/Philadelphia, 1990, pp.&nbsp;209–226.
